pr_title: fix(ivy): support inserting a `viewRef` that is already present
pr_body:
When inserting a `viewRef` it is possible to not provide
an `index`, which is regarded as appending to the end of
the container.

If the `viewRef` already exists in the container, then
this results in a move. But there was a fault in the logic
that computed where to insert the `viewRef` that did not
account for the fact that the `viewRef` was already in
the container, so the insertion `index` was outside the
bounds of the array.

Fixes #33924
pr_comments: I took your perf and test suggestions. Thanks @pkozlowski-opensource.

review_comments: Hmmm, this is interesting. Do you think that we could avoid doing any processing in the case where we "move" a view to the _same_ index? How about https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34054/files#diff-f0a30efe7a958f4c73731e33aa32ebfaR272-R283 instead?

I considered something similar to your suggestion but that would add yet more code to the bundle size...

I wasn't sure what the best trade off is. I guess the real question is how often would this happen. If we have change detection setup that constantly tries to insert a view into a container where it already exists (such as in ngx-formly), then this would indeed happen a lot.

BTW `index === undefined ? this.length - 1 : index)` is identical to `this._adjustIndex(index, -1)`

> BTW index === undefined ? this.length - 1 : index) is identical to this._adjustIndex(index, -1)

Right! 

> I considered something similar to your suggestion but that would add yet more code to the bundle size...

Hmm, as far as I can tell the total of added code would amount to `if (a !== b)` (after minification) so I would consider it as "worth it". Not married to the idea, though! 

Pushed an update to https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/34054
